pr.title: feat(gemm): opt-in flag to keep the SM120 FP4 GEMM autotuner off stream-K tactics
pr.body:
## 📌 Description

On SM120, `CutlassFp4GemmRunner::getConfigs()` (`fp4_gemm_cutlass_template_sm120.h`) gives each of the 8 tile shapes four configs: two data-parallel and two stream-K. The autotuner sees all 32 tactics and picks by time. A stream-K tactic sums a tile's K range in more than one CTA, so its output can differ in the last bits from the data-parallel tactics of the same shape.

This matters when the choice changes between processes. In vLLM 0.32.0 (which re-tunes `fp4_gemm` at every start) serving Qwen3-8B-NVFP4 on an RTX 5090, 8 fresh starts gave two different greedy outputs for the same 16 prompts. The start that differed was the only one that picked tactic 6 (128x32x128, stream-K) instead of tactic 4 (same tile, data-parallel) for the attention output projection at M = 1. With all other tactic choices fixed, switching only that entry between 4 and 6 moved the output between the two versions in both directions. vllm-project/vllm#62820 reports the same symptom on Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4, and an independent reproduction there (2026-10-26) traced it to the autotuner moving one `fp4_gemm` call (M = 252, down projection) to stream-K tactic 22; forcing tactic 21 (same tile, data-parallel) restored the untuned output. That comment asks for "a way to keep Stream-K tactics out of `fp4_gemm` tuning when reproducibility matters", which is what this flag is; the workaround suggested there, `VLLM_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_SKIP_OPS=fp4_gemm`, gives up tuning among the data-parallel tactics as well.

This PR adds `FLASHINFER_FP4_GEMM_DISABLE_STREAM_K`. When it is set to 1, the SM120 CUTLASS FP4 runner offers the autotuner only its 16 data-parallel tactics, and its new `validate_tactic` rejects a stream-K tactic loaded from a saved autotune cache, so a cache written before the flag was set cannot bring stream-K back. The autotuner treats such an entry as a miss: during autotuning it re-tunes the entry, and outside autotuning the call takes the untuned default (with `backend="cutlass"`, the runner's default data-parallel config). The default is unchanged, and the flag does not affect the SM100/SM103 runners. Any other value, or no value, keeps all 32 tactics.

`validate_tactic` also rejects a cached tactic index outside the runner's config list, for example one from a module with more configs. Such an entry is re-tuned instead of reaching the C++ check. This range check is in the factory the CUTLASS FP4 runners share, so it applies to all of them. Each runner counts its configs once, since `validate_tactic` runs on every cache hit.

Measured on an RTX 5090 with FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1 and the same change applied, unless a row says otherwise:

| check | result |
|---|---|
| All 432 FP4 GEMM calls of a Qwen3-8B-NVFP4 generation, every tactic run on vLLM's own operands | with the flag, the 16 offered tactics return identical bits on every call; stream-K tactics differ from them on 3 calls |
| vLLM greedy output over fresh starts, 16 prompts x 200 tokens | default: 2 different outputs in 8 starts; with the flag: 1 output in 31 starts |
| Same, autotune cache emptied before each of 16 starts (`VLLM_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_CACHE_DIR`) | default: 2 outputs with FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1 (the 16 starts split 9 and 7), 4 outputs with 0.7.2.post1; with the flag (this PR's branch built from source): 1 output in 16 starts, and none of the 16 saved caches holds a stream-K tactic |
| vLLM generate time, same workload | 15.1-16.2 s with the flag, 15.6-17.4 s default (not a paired benchmark) |

At M = 16 and 128 it also requires some stream-K tactic to differ from them on the generated operands, so the bit-equality check is shown able to fail. +"""CPU checks for FLASHINFER_FP4_GEMM_DISABLE_STREAM_K on the SM120 FP4 runner."""
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+
+import flashinfer.gemm.gemm_base as gemm_base
+
+
+def _runner(monkeypatch, with_export, calls=None):
+    module = SimpleNamespace(fp4_gemm=None, fp4_gemm_tactic_num=lambda: 8)
+    if with_export:
+
+        def is_stream_k(tactic):
+            if calls is not None:
+                calls.append(tactic)
+            # Among tactics 0 to 7, CutlassFp4GemmRunner::getConfigs() marks 2, 3, 6
+            # and 7 as stream-K. This stand-in marks 2 and 5, so the tests fail if the
+            # runner applies a tactic % 4 >= 2 rule instead of asking the module.
+            return tactic in (2, 5)
+
+        module.fp4_gemm_tactic_is_stream_k = is_stream_k
+    spec = SimpleNamespace(build_and_load=lambda: module)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(gemm_base, "gen_gemm_sm120_module_cutlass_fp4", lambda: spec)
+    gemm_base.get_gemm_sm120_module_cutlass_fp4.cache_clear()
+    runner = gemm_base.get_gemm_sm120_module_cutlass_fp4().cutlass_fp4_gemm_runner()
+    gemm_base.get_gemm_sm120_module_cutlass_fp4.cache_clear()
+    return runner
+
+
+@pytest.mark.cpu_only
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("with_export", [True, False])
+def test_flag_unset_keeps_every_tactic(monkeypatch, with_export):
+    monkeypatch.delenv("FLASHINFER_FP4_GEMM_DISABLE_STREAM_K", raising=False)
+    calls = []
+    runner = _runner(monkeypatch, with_export, calls)
+    assert runner.get_valid_tactics([], None) == list(range(8))
+    assert runner.validate_tactic([], 2)
+    # With the flag unset, fp4_gemm_tactic_is_stream_k is never called.
+    assert calls == []
+
+
+@pytest.mark.cpu_only
+def test_flag_set_uses_the_exported_classifier(monkeypatch):
+    monkeypatch.setenv("FLASHINFER_FP4_GEMM_DISABLE_STREAM_K", "1")
+    runner = _runner(monkeypatch, with_export=True)
+    runner_hash = hash(runner)
+    assert runner.get_valid_tactics([], None) == [0, 1, 3, 4, 6, 7]
+    # Building the stream-K set must not change hash(runner), which keys the
+    # in-process autotune cache.
+    assert hash(runner) == runner_hash
+    assert not runner.validate_tactic([], 5)
+    assert runner.validate_tactic([], 3)
+    assert runner.validate_tactic([], -1)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.cpu_only
+def test_flag_set_on_a_module_without_the_export_raises(monkeypatch):
+    monkeypatch.setenv("FLASHINFER_FP4_GEMM_DISABLE_STREAM_K", "1")

+def _nvfp4_operands_wide_range(m, n, k, seed):
+    # Log-normal magnitudes, seeded so a run is repeatable. With plain randn operands,
+    # every SM120 tactic returned the same bits at this test's shapes, stream-K
+    # included (RTX 5090 and RTX 5060 Ti). A test built on them could not tell a
+    # data-parallel tactic from a stream-K one. With the magnitudes spread over
+    # several powers of two (sigma 2.5), the stream-K tactics return different bits
+    # on most seeds. Narrower and wider spreads were measured to be worse.
+    gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(seed)

+    b = torch.randn([n, k], device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32, generator=gen)
+    a = (a * torch.exp(2.5 * torch.randn(a.shape, device="cuda", generator=gen))).to(
+        torch.bfloat16
+    )
+    b = (b * torch.exp(2.5 * torch.randn(b.shape, device="cuda", generator=gen))).to(

     "m,n,out_dtype,backend,use_nvfp4,auto_tuning",
     [
@@ -794,6 +821,84 @@ def test_mm_fp4_per_token_alpha_low_m_untuned(m, n, k, res_dtype):
     _check_per_token_alpha_untuned(m, n, k, res_dtype)
 
 
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("m", [1, 16, 128])
+def test_mm_fp4_cutlass_sm120_disable_stream_k(m, monkeypatch):
+    # With FLASHINFER_FP4_GEMM_DISABLE_STREAM_K=1 the SM120 CUTLASS runner offers the
+    # autotuner only data-parallel tactics. On wide-dynamic-range operands they all
+    # return the same bits, and the stream-K tactics do not. So the test checks both
+    # halves: the offered set agrees, and the excluded set would not have. The second
+    # half is checked from m = 16 up. At m = 1 the stream-K tactics differed on only
+    # 2 of 24 seeds on an RTX 5090 and 1 of 24 on a 36-SM RTX 5060 Ti, so a control
+    # there would be flaky.
+    from flashinfer.gemm import gemm_base
+
+    if not is_sm12x_supported(torch.device("cuda")):
+        pytest.skip("The SM120 CUTLASS FP4 GEMM needs SM12x.")
+    n, k = 4096, 4096
+    workspace = torch.empty(
+        gemm_base.DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_SIZE, device="cuda", dtype=torch.uint8
+    )
+    runner = gemm_base.get_gemm_sm120_module_cutlass_fp4().cutlass_fp4_gemm_runner()
+
+    def run(operands, tactic):
+        a_fp4, a_s, b_fp4, b_s, alpha = operands
+        alpha = torch.tensor([alpha], device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)
+        out = torch.empty([m, n], device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        inputs = [a_fp4, b_fp4.T, a_s, b_s.T, alpha, None, out, None, None, workspace]
+        runner(inputs=inputs, tactic=tactic)
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        return out
+
+    monkeypatch.delenv("FLASHINFER_FP4_GEMM_DISABLE_STREAM_K", raising=False)
+    all_tactics = runner.get_valid_tactics([], None)
+    for value in ("0", "", "false", "true"):
+        monkeypatch.setenv("FLASHINFER_FP4_GEMM_DISABLE_STREAM_K", value)
+        assert runner.get_valid_tactics([], None) == all_tactics
+    monkeypatch.setenv("FLASHINFER_FP4_GEMM_DISABLE_STREAM_K", "1")
+    tactics = runner.get_valid_tactics([], None)
+    # Two of the four configs of each tile shape are data-parallel.
+    assert len(tactics) == len(all_tactics) // 2 and set(tactics) < set(all_tactics)
+    # a stream-K tactic loaded from a saved autotune cache is rejected too
+    excluded = sorted(set(all_tactics) - set(tactics))
+    assert not any(runner.validate_tactic([], t) for t in excluded)
+    assert all(runner.validate_tactic([], t) for t in tactics + [-1])
+    # an index past the end of the config list is rejected, not passed to C++
+    assert not runner.validate_tactic([], len(all_tactics))
+
+    # Several seeds: whether a stream-K tactic rounds differently depends on the
+    # operands. At m = 16, 2 of 24 seeds showed no difference on an RTX 5090 and 7 of
+    # 24 on a 36-SM RTX 5060 Ti; at m = 128, 1 of 24 on both. So the equality half is
+    # checked on every seed tried. The negative control draws seeds until one shows a
+    # stream-K difference: four seeds always, then up to eight more while none has
+    # differed. A part where the first four happen to agree then does not fail a
+    # healthy test.
+    stream_k_differs = False
+    first_seed, min_seeds, max_seeds = 20261029, 4, 12
+    for i in range(max_seeds):
+        if i >= min_seeds and (m < 16 or stream_k_differs):
+            break
+        seed = first_seed + i
+        operands = _nvfp4_operands_wide_range(m, n, k, seed)
+        ref = run(operands, tactics[0])
+        for t in tactics[1:]:
+            assert torch.equal(run(operands, t), ref), (
+                f"tactic {t} differs from tactic {tactics[0]} (seed {seed})"
+            )
+        if m >= 16:
+            stream_k_differs |= any(
+                not torch.equal(run(operands, t), ref) for t in excluded
+            )
+    # Negative control: the same equality over the excluded stream-K tactics must fail
+    # on some seed, or the operands could not have told a stream-K tactic apart from a
+    # data-parallel one and the assertion above would be empty.
+    if m >= 16:
+        assert stream_k_differs, (
+            f"every stream-K tactic matched the data-parallel output on all {max_seeds} "
+            "seeds; the operands do not expose the summation order, so the equality check "
+            "above could not fail"
+        )
+
+
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     pytest.main([__file__])

comments.body: CodeRabbit points to #7207, which adds a general opt-in for the same problem (an `is_batch_invariant_tactic` hook on runners plus `FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, first used for MXFP8 split-K). The two fit together: the stream-K test here, `tactic % 4 >= 2`, is exactly what the SM120 FP4 runner would return as not batch-invariant. This PR does not depend on #7207, so it can go in on its own. If #7207 lands first, or you prefer the general mode, I can change this PR to implement `is_batch_invariant_tactic` on the SM120 runner and drop `FLASHINFER_FP4_GEMM_DISABLE_STREAM_K`.

Some data from a small SM120 part (RTX 5060 Ti, 36 SMs), at the Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 linear shapes (TP=2 per GPU, plus the TP=1 down projection from vllm#62820). PR head `1bccea78a`, CUDA 13.3, torch 2.13.0+cu130. All 32 tactics were timed with CUDA graphs on a cold L2 (CUDA-event timing; CUPTI was not installed at the time, edited for accuracy).

**1. The DP-only set is deterministic here too.** With wide-dynamic-range operands, all 16 data-parallel tactics gave bit-identical output in every case I tried (4 shapes x M = 1-252). The stream-K tactics split into up to 10 different results (for example, the TP=2 down projection at M = 128). So the premise of the flag holds on 36 SMs as well.

**2. The new test may not be able to fail.** With `_nvfp4_operands` (plain `randn`), all 32 tactics, stream-K included, are bit-identical at every shape I ran. My guess is that the FP4 products have so few significant bits that the FP32 accumulation never rounds, so the summation order does not matter. At the test's own shape (n = k = 4096):

| m | operands | DP tactics differing from tactic 0 | SK tactics differing |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | randn | none | none |
| 16 | randn | none | none |
| 16 | log-normal magnitudes | none | 26, 31 |
| 128 | log-normal magnitudes | none | 26, 31 |

The log-normal operands were `x = randn(s) * exp(2.5 * randn(s))`. With them, the DP-only equality assertion still passes, and the same assertion over all 32 tactics fails, which gives the test a negative control. Maybe use such operands for this test, or add an all-tactics negative-control assertion, so that it would catch a stream-K tactic slipping into the DP set. (On a 5090 the result may differ, since stream-K decomposition depends on the SM count.)

**3. Cost on a small part.** The flag costs more on some layers than the "same tile, data-parallel" framing suggests. The best DP tactic vs the best overall:

| layer (per GPU) | M = 1-16 | M = 64 | M = 252 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TP=2 down (5120 x 8704) | +13-20% | +28% | +13% |
| TP=2 attention qkv (7168 x 5120) | +7-12% | +2% | +6% |
| TP=2 GDN in_proj (8192 x 5120) | +1-3% | +1% | 0 |
| TP=2 gate_up (17408 x 5120) | 0 | 0 | +1% |
| TP=1 down (5120 x 17408) | +2-3% | +2% | +22% |

Summed over the 64 layers, that is about +2-4% of total NVFP4 GEMM time per step (decode M = 1: 11.45 to 11.71 ms per GPU), because gate_up dominates and does not care. That is a reasonable price for reproducibility, but a notable one for the down projection, so off by default seems right.

**4. Flips are plausible on 36 SMs too.** For the TP=1 down projection at M = 2-252, the tactics within 3% of the best span 2 to 6 different bit-classes, so a re-tune at every start can flip outputs here as well.

`tests/gemm/test_mm_fp4.py -k disable_stream_k`: 2 passed on this card.

(AI-assisted measurement and write-up; I checked the numbers on our own hardware.)
Made changes to address point 2 of https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/7819#issuecomment-6512439302

Checked `50501f232` on the RTX 5060 Ti (SM120, 36 SMs):

- `test_mm_fp4_cutlass_sm120_disable_stream_k` passes for m = 1, 16, 128.
- As a control, I swapped `_nvfp4_operands_wide_range` for plain `randn` operands (what the first version used). With that swap the negative control fires at m = 16 and 128 ("every stream-K tactic matched..."), so the test now fails when the operands can't distinguish a stream-K tactic from a data-parallel one.

Per-seed numbers on this card, for comparison with the 5090 figures in the test comment (24 seeds from 20261029, n = k = 4096, 16 DP + 16 SK tactics):

| m | DP tactics disagree | seeds where all SK tactics match DP |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | 0 / 24 | 23 / 24 |
| 16 | 0 / 24 | 7 / 24 |
| 128 | 0 / 24 | 1 / 24 |

Two small notes:

1. At m = 16 the control is weaker here than on the 5090 (7 of 24 seeds show no difference, vs. 2 of 24). The four fixed seeds in the test still include differing ones on this card. A part where all four happen to match would fail the control even though nothing is wrong, though. More seeds, or stopping at the first seed that differs, would add margin.
2. The comment says m = 1 differed on "none tried on a 36-SM RTX 5060 Ti". With these 24 seeds, one does differ at m = 1. Skipping the control there is still right; only the wording is slightly off.

(AI-assisted measurement and write-up; I checked the numbers on our own hardware.)
Thanks. Both notes were taken in cd97fd827.

Rechecked `cd97fd827` on the RTX 5060 Ti (36 SMs): `test_mm_fp4_cutlass_sm120_disable_stream_k` passes for m = 1, 16, 128. With plain `randn` operands swapped in, m = 16 and 128 still fail with the new "matched ... on all 12 seeds" message, so the extra seeds didn't weaken the control. Thanks for taking both notes.

(AI-assisted measurement and write-up; I checked the numbers on our own hardware.)

@jimmyzho 

Thanks for checking whether `batch_invariant=True` reaches SM120, and for the two requests.

Both are done in 8254b08e4:

1. Docs row. The `FLASHINFER_FP4_GEMM_DISABLE_STREAM_K` row now says that `mm_fp4(..., batch_invariant=True)` is the supported route where it exists (SM100 / SM103 / SM107). It says this flag covers SM12x only, since SM120 and SM121 load the same module. The row no longer states tactic counts, because the layout now lives only in C++.

2. Stream-K classifier. The SM120 binding exports `fp4_gemm_tactic_is_stream_k(tactic)`. It returns `use_stream_k` from `getFp4GemmConfig`, the lookup `fp4_gemm` itself uses. That config does not depend on the problem shape, so the function takes only the tactic. The runner reads it on first use, and only when the flag is `1`. The Python `tactic % 4 >= 2` rule is gone. Because the classifier and `fp4_gemm` now read the same list, a change to `getConfigs()` cannot put them out of step, so the mismatch you describe can no longer happen. What CI still cannot check without an SM120 lane is the real binding itself: that runs only in `test_mm_fp4_cutlass_sm120_disable_stream_k` on SM120 hardware, as before.

One behaviour comes with the export. A module built by an older FlashInfer (for example an installed jit-cache) has no `fp4_gemm_tactic_is_stream_k`. With the flag unset, such a module runs every tactic as before. With the flag set, a tuning run raises a `RuntimeError` that names the missing function. A cached tactic other than the default `-1` then fails revalidation, so the flag cannot quietly let stream-K tactics through. The docs row says this.

Tests on an RTX 5090 (SM120):
- `tests/gemm/test_mm_fp4.py -k "disable_stream_k or cutlass or backend_auto"`: 6 passed, including `test_mm_fp4_cutlass_sm120_disable_stream_k[1/16/128]`; 4 skipped (`backend="auto"` is not supported on compute capability 12.0).
- New `tests/cpu/gemm/test_sm120_fp4_stream_k_flag.py`: 5 passed. Its stand-in module marks tactics 2 and 5 as stream-K, which is not the real layout, so the tests fail if the runner stops asking the module. They check that:
  - with the flag unset, every tactic is kept, for a module with and without the export (two tests);
  - with the flag set, the exported classifier decides, and building the set leaves the runner's hash (the key of the in-process autotune cache) unchanged;
  - a module without the export raises;
  - a runner with no classifier (the SM100 and SM103 path) ignores the flag.
- pre-commit (clang-format, ruff, mypy) passes on the changed files.

Your review says 1c14bd693 "covers the two small points from my side", and the inline comment says "Still open from last round". I can't find an earlier review or comment from you on this PR. Was there a pending review that wasn't submitted, or another thread I should read?

I agree with your reading of what the flag promises: it removes only the stream-K vs data-parallel disagreement. The docs row says that agreement among the data-parallel tactics is measured, not guaranteed, and it makes no batch-invariance claim.

On approval: that decision belongs to the maintainers who steered #7207, and I will wait for their view. I'm glad to go either way: keep this as an opt-in, SM12x-only flag, or work toward an SM120 class in the batch-invariant mode.
